case_title: Dandu Jaggaraju v. State of A.P.
victim_caste: Kshatriya (victim); husband was a member of the Scheduled Castes
weapon: None mentioned (death by smothering with the victim's chunni pushed into her mouth)
evidence_type: Last-seen (circumstantial) evidence, medical (post-mortem) evidence, recovery of jewellery, identification by witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: None noted (alleged family-honour motive was not accepted by the Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.302, 201 and 379; sentence amount not specified in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, a woman who had married a man against her family's wishes, lived with her husband and young child in a house owned by another family. About six years after the marriage, the accused, a paternal uncle of the victim, telephoned the victim on 14 August 2002, saying her grandmother was seriously ill and that he would come to pick her up. A household member was sent to a telephone booth to guide him. The accused arrived, was brought to the house, and was introduced by the victim as her uncle. The victim left with the accused on a white scooter, leaving her young son behind. Her husband returned that evening and was told she had gone with the accused. She did not return that night or the next day. The husband lodged a report on 16 August 2002 that she had gone to relatives and had not been seen since. Her body was recovered later that day. A second report then recorded the husband's suspicion, for the first time, that the accused had lured her away and killed her. A post-mortem found death by asphyxia due to smothering, with her scarf pushed into her mouth. The accused was arrested on 7 September 2002, and jewellery the victim was said to have been wearing when she disappeared was recovered from the accused's pockets. The prosecution relied on last-seen testimony from household members and a press reporter who saw the victim and the accused at a bus stand, on the jewellery recovery, and on the post-mortem findings. Witnesses who had seen the accused gave statements to a magistrate about four months later, and one witness identified the accused in court more than two years after the event.
physical_harm: Death by asphyxia due to smothering
financial_property_loss: Alleged loss of victim's jewellery (ornaments); the Court described them as 'disco jewellery' of trifling value
premeditation_planning: Not found by the Court; prosecution alleged the victim was lured away under a pretext
motive: alleged: family annoyance at the victim's marriage to a member of the Scheduled Castes, against family wishes (family honour); the Court found the motive clearly suspect and did not accept it
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted as connecting the accused. The Court found last-seen evidence uncertain and the jewellery recovery unbelievable; post-mortem cause of death was recorded but did not link the accused to the crime
witness_credibility: Last-seen witnesses (P.Ws. 2, 3, 6) found uncertain: late s.164 statements, no test identification parade, and P.W.6 knew the accused only by sight and first identified him in court two and a half years later
post_offence_conduct: Prosecution alleged the accused carried the victim's jewellery until arrest 24 days later; the Court found this completely unacceptable and not credible
custody_duration: In custody from arrest on 7 September 2002; still in custody at the time of the Supreme Court judgment
trial_duration: offence: 14 August 2002; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 20 February 2007; Supreme Court: 20 July 2011
legal_representation: Accused: Siddharth Dave (Amicus) with Jemtiben A.o.; State of Andhra Pradesh: D. Mahesh Babu, Ramesh Allanki, Savita Dhanda
investigation_status: Missing-person FIR 16 Aug 2002; second FIR after body recovery; investigation completed; accused arrested 7 Sept 2002 and tried
procedural_irregularity: No test identification parade held; s.164 statements recorded about four months after the incident
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.302, 201, 379 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, accused acquitted
prosecution_argument: Last-seen evidence and jewellery recoveries together formed a complete chain; concurrent findings of guilt should not be disturbed
defence_argument: No evidence connected the accused to the crime; the first report was of a missing person with no suspicion expressed; apart from last-seen evidence, recoveries could not be believed; the chain was missing
legal_principle_applied: In circumstantial cases each link, including motive, must be proved; last-seen evidence, identification and recovery (including s.27 disclosure) must be reliable
other_sentence_order: Accused to be released forthwith if not wanted in any other case; Amicus fee fixed at Rs. 7,000
